extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A freely and publicly available benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification created by Northwestern Polytechnical University. It contains 31,500 remote sensing images divided into 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class. Images are 256×256 pixels in RGB color space and cover more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu. Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by first selecting representative scene classes. The authors investigated all scene classes of existing datasets to form 30 widely used scene categories, then searched keywords including "OBIA", "GEOBIA", "land cover classification", "land use classification", "geographic image retrieval", and "geospatial object detection" on Web of Science and Google Scholar to carefully select 15 meaningful scene classes, resulting in 45 scene classes. The images were extracted by experts in remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions worldwide and were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Remote sensing images extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by superimposing images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) data onto a 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were extracted from Google Earth and organized into 45 scene classes, with each class including 700 images. Each image was formatted to 256×256 pixels in RGB color space.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each image in the dataset has a size of 256×256 pixels in the red green blue (RGB) color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene labels correspond to 45 selected scene classes. The dataset was extracted by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation, and images were assigned to scene classes such as airplane, airport, baseball diamond, basketball court, beach, bridge, chaparral, church, circular farmland, cloud, commercial area, dense residential, desert, forest, freeway, golf course, ground track field, harbor, industrial area, intersection, island, lake, meadow, medium residential, mobile home park, mountain, overpass, palace, parking lot, railway, railway station, rectangular farmland, river, roundabout, runway, sea ice, ship, snowberg, sparse residential, stadium, storage tank, tennis court, terrace, thermal power station, and wetland.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The creation of this dataset will enable the community to develop and evaluate various new data-driven algorithms, at a much larger scale, to further improve the state of the art in remote sensing image scene classification.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper discusses limitations of existing datasets rather than explicit limitations of NWPU-RESISC45. Existing datasets are described as having small scale of scene classes and image numbers, lack of image variations and diversity, and saturation of classification accuracy. For NWPU-RESISC45, some classes such as island, lake, mountain, and snowberg have lower spatial resolutions than most other classes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is proposed as a benchmark for remote sensing image scene classification and is intended to enable the community to develop and evaluate various data-driven algorithms. In the paper it is used for training and testing scene classification methods under 10%-90% and 20%-80% train-test splits, and results are reported as useful performance baselines for future research.
